From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Brandy

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
brandy
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

    Shortened form of brandywine, from Dutch brandewijn (“burnt wine”). Compare German Brantewein, Branntwein, Danish brændevin.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • enPR: brănʹdē, IPA(key): /ˈbɹændi/
    • Audio (Southern England):(file)
    • Rhymes: -ændi

    Noun

    [edit]

    brandy (countable and uncountable, plural brandies)

    2. (uncountable) An alcoholic liquor distilled from wine or fermented fruit juice.
      Synonym: eau de vie (brandy sense)
      Hyponyms: cognac, aqua vitae, eau de vie (hardest sense)
    3. (countable) Any variety of such liquor.
    4. (countable) A serving of such liquor.

    Verb

    [edit]

    brandy (third-person singular simple present brandies, present participle brandying, simple past and past participle brandied)

    1. (transitive) To preserve, flavour, or mix with brandy.
